newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-INDIA GDRS EDGE UPWARD IN THIN TRADE.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-INDIA GDRS EDGE UPWARD IN THIN TRADE.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts gained in thin trading on Tuesday, despite losses in local markets.
Bombay's main index fell 53.94 points to 4,427.36 in anticipation of an announcement that expected stock market reforms would be delayed.
After the close of local trading, the Securities and Exchange Board of India said that mooted changes in carry-forward trading would not be considered until September.
GDR investors took the news in stride, dealers said.
"They still think its going to come through but it has been delayed a little. The local market overreacted," a dealer said.
The HSBC James Capel India GDR index gained 0.76 points, or 0.88 percent, to 86.50, a premium of 19.79 percent to the local market.
The Cazenove Indian GDR index, which measures changes from midday to midday, was up 0.12 points at 97.46.
Blue chip Reliance gained 21 cents to $23.00/24.00, and Hindalco lost 12 cents to $34.75/$35.75.

The Capel Taiwan index was off 0.09 points, or 0.06 percent, at 137.52 -- representing a discount of 2.17 percent -- as weakness in electronics shares spread, dragging the home market down 89.53 to 9,807.36.
The Capel Korea index finished down 0.80 points, or 1.02 percent, at 77.73, a premium of 40.60 percent.
